status: Research/design only; no Unity implementation or physical-device tests.
confirmed_requirements: Every player travels independently among locations, rooms, and compatible story instances.
Entering another player's area joins the existing shared state; avatars become mutually visible subject to camera framing and intentional hiding.
One person's departure must not pause, reload, move, or reset the remaining players.
A particular bucket is one shared object with at most one current holder; pickup and release are visible to others.
proposed_implementation: Persistent world/network model separate from each client's presentation loading.
Stable world, zone, player and prop IDs; atomic zone transfer including carried props.
Explicit observer membership changes, dependency readiness, revisioned snapshots and state updates.
Server-owned props plus temporary per-item interaction reservations, idempotent commands and disconnect cleanup.
Independent visual unloading must not destroy authoritative state on a mobile listen host.
Prove two-zone travel, exclusive bucket use, late arrival, and host travel before expanding content.

sources.title: Unity NetworkSceneManager
sources.finding: Server scene events synchronize clients; distinguish local loading callbacks from completed network synchronization.

sources.title: Unity custom scene management
sources.finding: Custom scene handling needs readiness/synchronization logic; in-scene network objects have limitations. Use registered dynamic prefabs with deliberate lifetime.

sources.title: Unity object visibility
sources.finding: Per-client visibility; update NetworkShow/NetworkHide when membership changes. Hiding destroys the client's representation, not the authoritative world record.

sources.title: Unity NetworkVariables
sources.finding: Current values synchronize to late joiners; initialize from current state and subscribe to changes. Official page read directly after web extractor errors.

sources.title: Unity NetworkObject ownership
sources.finding: Server ownership in client-server topology and DontDestroyWithOwner lifetime option; neither implements the game's exclusive-hold protocol automatically.
